correctness.rationale: For every real periodic BV f the derivative signed measure has zero mass and admits a coupling of its Jordan parts. The Hilbert diameter bound reduces the sharp operator norm exactly to a two-atom pulse, and uniqueness follows from nonzero Fourier multipliers of -t G_t prime. The periodic Green kernel solves (I-t Delta)G=delta; H=G*G=G+t partial_t G and H-second derivative produce the stated normalized objective and derivative. The sign is that of z coth z+2-a coth a, with strict monotonicity for z>0; this proves all-time global uniqueness. Expansions at a infinity and at a_c prove the short-time and critical laws. The current standalone checker verifies independent Fourier sums and root numerics with tail bounds; no numerical test replaces the proof.

value.rationale: The implicit-Euler heat step is a canonical positive regularizer. The all-time exact best BV-to-L2 constant and complete equality cases make a usable benchmark for discontinuous input data. The explicit transition a coth a=3, the unique short-pulse-to-semicircle change and the rigorous square-root critical exponent reveal a global geometric effect not obtained from routine contractivity bounds or mere positive-kernel identities. This is a complete natural parameter classification, not a numerical increment or arbitrary isolated degree.
